verdict.rationale: cubic's own Custom agents feature lets teams write review rules that enforce their best practices across pull requests. These rules live in cubic.yaml and can be adopted from a community library, and cubic reviews new PRs automatically. A community comment confirms the rules are written in plain English. The evidence does not show these agents working as merge-gating pre-merge checks, nor rules like 'docs updated' or 'tests cover new paths'. missing for 10: documentation that custom agents run as blocking pre-merge status checks, evidence of rules like 'docs updated' or 'tests cover new paths', first-party documentation that rules are written in plain language, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I define custom agentic pre-merge checks in plain language — 'docs updated', 'tests cover new paths' — that run on every PR

citations.quote: Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
plain-English rules kept in the codebase
